summary: Round 2 verification of Task 7 fixes. SEC-T7-001 was reopened: the redaction guard checks typeof opts.body === 'object', but by the time ofetch's FetchError is constructed the body has already been replaced with a serialized JSON string ('{"token":"<real-token>"}'), so the guard is falsy and the branch never runs — the token still leaks through err.options.body for any caller that logs the error. response.status and other fields are unaffected by the (no-op) mutation; undefined-body is correctly skipped by the short-circuit. SEC-T7-002 and SEC-T7-003 acknowledged as skipped per Round 1 decisions and not re-litigated.

findings.owasp: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures / CWE-532 Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
findings.category: A09 — Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.title: Redaction guard never matches — token still leaks in FetchError.options.body
findings.description: The fix in commit 7a064dd attempts to redact the token by reassigning opts.body when err.options.body is a plain object: `if (opts && opts.body && typeof opts.body === 'object' && opts.body !== null) { opts.body = { ...(opts.body), token: '[redacted]' } }`. However, ofetch serialises the request body to a JSON string *before* dispatching the underlying fetch() call. Verified in node_modules/.pnpm/ofetch@1.5.1/.../shared/ofetch.CWycOUEr.mjs:236-242: when method is a payload method (POST here) and the body is JSON-serialisable (our `{ token }` is), ofetch executes `context.options.body = JSON.stringify(context.options.body)`. The fetch is then attempted on line 274; any failure (network error path on 278-286, or createFetchError on 191) constructs the FetchError *after* this mutation. FetchError exposes `options` via a getter that returns the live `ctx.options` (lines 24-30), so `err.options.body` is the serialised string '{"token":"<real-token>"}'. `typeof '...' === 'object'` is false → the redaction branch is skipped → the original (string) body remains on the error and is re-thrown with the secret intact. A caller that does `console.error(err)` or `Sentry.captureException(err)` (which serialises enumerable getters) will log the token verbatim. The fix has no effect on the only realistic failure paths.
findings.impact: Bearer-equivalent Telegram bot token (D17 secret) leaks to any error sink that serialises the rejected error — browser console in dev, Sentry/Datadog/LogRocket in prod, custom global error handlers, Nuxt's onErrorCaptured. An attacker with access to one of those sinks (or a developer pasting an error into a ticket) gains full control of the bot account: read all incoming messages, send messages as the bot, change the webhook URL to siphon traffic. Exactly the leak Round 1 set out to close; the Round 2 patch does not close it.
